title: Up, Up, Down
learning_objectives: Read a short book alone using the words up and down
Say what goes up and what comes down
parent_prompts: Let the child read alone. After: what went up? What came down? Which one stayed up?

pages.illustration_brief: Mo throws a red ball upward in a garden; ball high with motion lines.
pages.image_alt: Mo throws a red ball upward in a garden.

pages.illustration_brief: The ball bouncing on the grass near Mo.
pages.image_alt: The ball bouncing on the grass near Mo.

pages.illustration_brief: A yellow leaf lifted by a gust; wind lines.
pages.image_alt: A yellow leaf lifted by a gust.

pages.text: The leaf comes down. Slow, slow.
pages.illustration_brief: The leaf drifting down in a zigzag path.
pages.audio_script: The leaf comes down. Slow, slow.

vocabulary.definition: Not fast; taking a long time.

pages.image_alt: The leaf drifting down in a zigzag path.

pages.illustration_brief: A small brown bird flying up from a bush.
pages.image_alt: A small brown bird flying up from a bush.

pages.text: The bird does not come down. It sits in the tree. Bye, bird!
pages.illustration_brief: The bird perched high in a tree; Mo waving from the grass.
pages.audio_script: The bird does not come down. It sits in the tree. Bye, bird!
pages.image_alt: The bird perched high in a tree; Mo waving from the grass.

quiz.explanation: Page 4 says: The leaf comes down. Slow, slow.

quiz.prompt: Which one does not come down?
quiz.explanation: The ball comes down (page 2) and the leaf comes down (page 4), but the bird sits in the tree (page 6).

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up the three things that went up. Which one stayed up?
quiz.rubric: not yet: names one thing; with support: two things with prompting; independent: ball, leaf, bird, and says the bird stayed in the tree
quiz.explanation: Listing all three and the odd one out shows the pattern was followed.

off_screen_prompt: Throw a soft toy up and catch it. Then drop a tissue. Which comes down slower?
